ety.text: From Middle English fard, feard, ferd, ferde, fered, equivalent to fear + -ed.

senses.d: Pertaining to someone or thing that causes great fear in others.
Regarded with fear, respect, or reverence.
Frightened, afraid.
ex: Conſcience grows feared: the heart grows hardened: while you delay, the Devil rules and rejoyceth: […]
[…] I’m maist feared to speak to him—and it’s an unco thing to hear ane o’ us speak that gate o’ a man—[…]

ety.text: From feature + -ed.

senses.d: displayed with special treatment
ex: This month's featured products are on the first page of the catalogue.

senses.d: Having features of a particular kind.
ex: the broad-featured son of a farmer

grp.label: having features of a particular kind

ety.text: From an adjectival use of the past participle of definire.
Past participle of destacar.
